name: gigglybits-theme-lab
description: Design your own dark VS Code theme, preview it live, and give each project a color of its own.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with GigglyBits Theme Lab
walkthroughs.description: Design a dark theme, try it in one project, and choose the theme new windows use.

steps.title: Open the Theme Lab
steps.description:
Build a theme from one base color and a color rule, and see it on a whole VS Code window as you go.
[Open Theme Lab](command:gigglybits.openThemeLab)

steps.title: Try it in this project
steps.description: Step 1 alone makes a complete theme. Try in VS Code shows it in the project you have open, and Save theme keeps it.

steps.title: Choose your default theme
steps.description: New windows use your default theme. The Lab's first step shows which one that is, and Change default sets it.

gigglybits.library.markdownDescription: Your saved themes, written by **Save theme** in the Theme Lab (**GigglyBits: Open Theme Lab**). There is no limit on how many you keep. Each appears in the theme picker as `GigglyBits: <name>`, from the extension GigglyBits generates for them, GigglyBits Saved Themes. Use the Theme Lab or **GigglyBits: Choose Theme** rather than editing this by hand.

gigglybits.syntaxSets.markdownDescription: Your syntax sets, written by step 4 of the Theme Lab (**GigglyBits: Open Theme Lab**). A syntax set is a named set of code colors (keywords, functions, strings, tags and more) that a saved theme can use instead of its palette's, so code looks the same in every workspace. Use the Theme Lab rather than editing this by hand.

scripts.compile: npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.js
scripts.package: npm run check-types && npm run check-types:test && npm run lint && npm run themes:check && node esbuild.js --production && npm run smoke:bundle
scripts.verify: npm run check-types && npm run lint && npm test
scripts.clean: node -e "for (const d of ['dist', 'out']) require('fs').rmSync(d, { recursive: true, force: true })"
scripts.build:pack: npm run clean && npm run pack
scripts.dev:quick: npm run build:pack && npm run install:local
scripts.full:patch: npm run version:patch && npm run dev:quick
